rationale: The Garage Cam (CAM-S1) showed RSSI of -86 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections and delayed notifications, while all other devices and the base station were normal. Firmware was compatible (v3 supported) and battery was fine, ruling out other causes. Installing the RP-1 repeater resolved the issue, confirming weak signal as the root cause.

repair_steps: Confirm the RP-1 repeater is installed and powered on between the base station and the detached garage.
Verify the Garage Cam RSSI is now above -80 dBm (ideally above -70 dBm) in Device Settings > Device Info.
Ask the customer to monitor the Garage Cam for 24-48 hours to ensure it stays online without intermittent disconnections or delayed notifications.
If the issue recurs, check for new sources of interference or consider relocating the repeater or camera.
Document the resolution in the case notes and close the ticket.

results.text: Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.

Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.

results.text: Three sensors in different rooms went offline at the same minute; base station online, RSSI history normal, E-610 in log. Restarting did not help. Escalated; radio module replaced. Escalated correctly.
